page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-lssd-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 144 physical cores and 288 virtual cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 2232.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing 7.75 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it bundles 16242 GB of NVMe SSD capacity across 6 local SSDs. It does not include any GPUs.

Benchmark data shows top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 313266.86 and a PassMark CPU score of 178741.62. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 1090.21 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 412.25 GB/sec for write operations. The server excels in database operations, achieving 422.06 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and top-tier performance in PassMark database operations. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the average tier. LLM text generation speeds are also limited, with the 135M model text generation rated as poor.

Given its bare-metal architecture, massive memory capacity, and high-density local NVMe storage, this server offers high resource density for enterprise-scale workloads. The qualitative cost efficiency is aligned with its premium hardware class, trading off single-threaded efficiency for massive parallel processing capabilities and high-throughput memory access. This server is highly suited for large-scale database hosting, high-throughput Redis caching, memory-intensive data processing, and enterprise software compilation.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-lssd-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server featuring 288 vCPUs (144 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor at 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 2232.0 GB of DDR5 memory and 16242 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, with no integrated GPUs. The server delivers top-tier performance in multi-core CPU benchmarks, database operations, and memory bandwidth, although its single-core performance and LLM text generation speeds are average to poor. This high-density hardware profile is designed for memory-intensive, parallel workloads. It is best suited for large-scale database hosting, high-throughput caching systems like Redis, and enterprise software compilation.
